title: Strange botanical: Prism Lungwort After the Cloudburst
tests: Fictional strange botanical; dominant epilithic colony; inflated translucent rain-capture leaves; internal sapphire flowers; crown-vent silver capsules releasing silk-parachute seeds; limestone sinkhole cloud-forest field photography; clear growth stages; no text, poster layout, fantasy glow, fungus, or horror.
prompt:
Create a finished square strange-botanical field photograph titled "Prism Lungwort After the Cloudburst." This is an invented plant species, shown as if documented in a remote limestone sinkhole cloud forest immediately after heavy rain. Make one mature colony dominate the frame at thumbnail scale: dozens of large, paired, translucent leaves rise directly from wet limestone cracks and inflate into ribbed lung-like lantern forms, each leaf 30 to 60 centimeters tall, pale celadon at the base and clear rose-amber toward the crown. The anatomy must remain unmistakably botanical: strong central veins, fine branching venation, pleated leaf ribs, waxy cuticle, water droplets, torn older leaf margins, and dense reddish root mats gripping mineral seams. The inflated leaves capture rain and fog; show pooled water and tiny air bubbles inside their translucent chambers, with soft daylight refracting through them rather than magical self-illumination.

Reveal the reproductive system clearly within the same natural scene. Several mature leaf chambers contain small sapphire-blue flowers suspended on thin green pedicels, visible through the leaf walls. At the crown, narrow vent-like slits have opened around silver-gray seed capsules. A fresh gust sends a concentrated plume of delicate silk-parachute seeds out through these crown vents and across the upper third of the frame, while a few capsules remain split open and others are still closed. Keep the flower, capsule, vent, seed, and leaf relationships physically connected and readable. Younger flat leaves cluster near the roots; mid-stage leaves are half-inflated; old collapsed leaves lie papery and translucent against the stone, showing a believable growth cycle without becoming a diagram.

Photograph from knee height with a weather-sealed full-frame camera and 45 mm macro-capable lens, close enough that the dominant inflated rosette fills two-thirds of the image while the colony continues up the curved sinkhole wall. Use soft overcast daylight filtering through a circular canopy opening, cool mist in the far background, and crisp wet-surface detail in the foreground. Include pitted ivory limestone, calcite veins, moss cushions, tiny ferns, wet leaf litter, trickling rivulets, mineral grit caught in roots, and one ordinary small snail on the rock for scale. Palette: wet limestone ivory, deep moss green, celadon, rose amber, sapphire blue, silver seed husks, and soft gray mist. Rich natural texture, restrained color, believable depth of field, slightly imperfect field framing, subtle sensor grain, and no studio backdrop.

The result must look like an extraordinary but credible botanical discovery whose growth strategy and reproduction are visible at a glance, not a fantasy illustration, alien landscape, carnivorous plant, mutation horror, fungus, glass sculpture, decorative lamps, or product display. No people, tools, labels, captions, poster panels, specimen board, readable text, arrows, borders, watermark, glowing magic, faces, eyes, mouths, blood, gore, or humanoid anatomy.
